name: prose-bible
description: Per-project continuity for prose: a bible of characters, terms, timeline and metaphors; a cross-file index with locations; a critic that flags contradictions it can cite in two places.

interface.shortDescription: Keeps a project's characters, terms and timeline straight, and flags contradictions it can cite in two places.
interface.longDescription: One skill and one read-only critic. prose-bible proposes bible entries from a deterministic cross-file index (names, defined terms, dates, numbers, repeated passages, each with file, line and offset), which the writer confirms one by one; entries persist per project in the shared writing-identity registry with undo, and nothing is saved without approval. prose-continuity-critic reads the index's diff and the bible in a clean context and reports a term defined two ways, an attribute that drifted, an anecdote retold — every finding citing both locations, or dropped. It never guesses a location the index did not supply, never scores, and never states or implies who wrote anything. NOTE: Codex enforces neither the critic's read-only tool restriction nor context isolation; run it as a fresh `codex exec` over the index and bible rather than inline.
defaultPrompt: Build the bible for this novel from the chapters so far
Did I contradict myself anywhere across these essays?
Which terms have I defined more than one way?
Show me every place Mara's eyes are described
